title: SDK Regression Response Lab and Hotfix Templates
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Overview:

This playbook describes an operational lab and step-by-step response process for SDK regressions that impact customer integrations. It bundles: a reproducible regression-harness (golden trace + delta runner), telemetry sentinel checks, a fastpatch template set (patch + release gating), and the docs-site hotpatch procedure.

Purpose and scope:
- Provide a single source-of-truth runbook for triage engineers and SDK owners when a surfaced regression affects generation, streaming, or embeddings clients.
- Cover detection -> local repro -> blocked-release mitigation -> postmortem.
- Include templates for GitHub PRs, release notes, canary config, and docs-site patches.

When to use:
1) High-severity regressions (P1/P2) seen in production error rate, user-facing behavior regressions, or breaking changes in public SDK API.
2) Recurring defects detected by golden diff runs after a runtime or infra change.

Key SLA & ownership:
- On-call / Triage response time: 30 minutes to acknowledge (eng-sre).
- Initial mitigation (customer-impacting fallback or rollback) within 2 hours.
- Root-cause and RCA published in Confluence within 5 business days.
- Ownership: SDK primary owner (developer experience) + eng-sre for runtime/infra issues.

Prerequisites (local lab):
- Local delta runner: repo devx/regression-runner (checkout at origin/devx).
- Golden traces: s3://redwood-goldens/sdk-traces/YYYY/*.jsonl
- Telemetry access: honeycomb/traces-prod read + observability dashboard link.
- Dev environment: Node 18 / Python 3.11 + Docker 24.

Runbook summary (ordered):
1. Detect & triage
   - Confirm alert source: SLO dashboard, customer report, or CI golden delta.
   - Capture failure signatures: error codes, stack traces, request IDs, sample prompts.
   - Create an incident doc (oncall/incident-process/runbook template).

2. Reproduce locally (delta-runner flow)
   - Pull latest golden archive and sample failed requests.
   - Run:

     docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work -w /work ghcr.io/redwood/devx/delta-runner:latest 
       --golden s3://redwood-goldens/sdk-traces/stable.jsonl 
       --candidate ./my-build/output.jsonl 
       --mode compare 
       --output ./delta-report.json

   - Expected outputs: delta-report.json with buckets: behavior-deltas, latency-regressions, token-diff-summary.

3. Telemetry sentinel checks
   - Run the sentinel query against the last 24h window:

     query: SELECT count(*) FROM sdk_errors WHERE customer_tier = 'prod' AND error_code IN ('STREAM_TIMEOUT','INVALID_RESPONSE')

   - Thresholds: if error rate > 0.5% of requests for top-tier customers, escalate to P1.

4. Mitigation options (choose one based on scope)
   - Hot rollback: revert the last deploy (use infra rollback checklist).
   - Runtime fallback: flip config to fallback-compatible model variant by tag (routing policy change).
   - Client-side patch: ship a short-lived client-side validation SDK patch (see fastpatch templates).

5. Fix & validate
   - Produce a patch branch with unit + regression golden tests.
   - Run full integration through delta-runner and staged canary.
   - Promote to main only after golden diffs are within acceptable thresholds (see Golden Acceptance Criteria).

Golden Acceptance Criteria (example):
| Category | Metric | Threshold |
|---|---:|---:|
| Behavioral parity | % prompts with identical token prefix | >= 98% |
| Latency | p95 token latency delta | <= +10ms |
| Streaming | stream resume success rate | >= 99.5% |

Hotfix templates (copy & adapt):
- GitHub PR title: [hotfix/sdk] fix <area>: <short description> (regression)
- PR body sections required:
  1) Summary of regression and root-cause hypothesis
  2) Repro steps + delta-runner output path
  3) Tests added (unit/integration/goldens)
  4) Canary plan and rollback steps
  5) Related incident id and customer impact notes

Fastpatch example (Node SDK snippet for version pin + runtime guard):

const DEFAULT_COMPAT_VERSION = "1.7.3";
function safeCreateClient(opts) {
  if ((opts?.version ?? DEFAULT_COMPAT_VERSION) !== DEFAULT_COMPAT_VERSION) {
    console.warn('Using non-default SDK version; enabling safe-mode');
    opts.safeMode = true;
  }
  return new RedwoodClient(opts);
}

Canary & docs-site hotpatch sequence:
1) Create canary build with label canary/regression-<id>.
2) Deploy canary to internal beta region with 5% traffic and observability hooks.
3) If metrics pass for 2 hours (no error spike, token-diff within threshold), increase to 25% then 100%.
4) Meanwhile, author a docs-site emergency patch page under devx-snippets with the patch note and API contract clarification.
5) Docs-site publishing steps (atomic):
   - Create markdown patch under docs-repo/content/devx/patches/
   - Open PR referencing the hotfix PR and include a short rollback paragraph.
   - Use docs ci 'fast-sync' label to bypass long builds for emergency patches.

Top support issues & canonical fixes (common patterns):
- Symptom: Streaming truncated mid-response. Canonical fix: add resume-token guard + increase read timeout by 200ms; add golden streaming test.
- Symptom: Deterministic output drift after quantized model rollout. Canonical fix: add token-normalization shim and update quantization profile mapping; run delta-runner acceptance.
- Symptom: Auth failures from new SDK when proxy present. Canonical fix: fallback to legacy auth handshake in presence of PROXY_ENV and add telemetry tag proxy=true.

Post-incident checklist:
1) Create RCA and link delta-runner outputs + telemetry dashboards.
2) Publish customer-facing incident summary (if impacted) via customer-success templates.
3) Add regression to scheduled golden-run CI with a failing test to prevent recurrence.
4) Add a short-lived alert rule for the specific error signature for 30 days.

Appendix A — Sample delta-runner config (YAML):

pipeline:
  name: sdk-regression-compare
  inputs:
    - gold: s3://redwood-goldens/sdk-traces/stable.jsonl
    - candidate: ./artifacts/candidate.jsonl
  compare:
    - behavior: token-prefix-compare
    - streaming: resume-token-check
  outputs:
    - delta-report.json
    - histogram.png

Appendix B — Quick telemetry queries (Honeycomb/Traces):
- Errors by version:
  dataset=traces service=sdk-prod | group_by(version) | count()
- Streaming resume failures last 1h:
  dataset=traces service=sdk-prod | filter(event='stream_resume_failure') | count()

Related links and references:
- SDK regression runner (internal repo): https://git.internal/redwood/devx/regression-runner
- Dev docs hotpatch policy: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/docs-site-emergency-patch-and-rollback-playbook-2026
- Incident template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/incident-template

Owner & maintenance:
- Primary owner: Developer Experience (SDK) team.
- Secondary owner: eng-sre (monitoring & sentinel configuration).
- Review cadence: annually or after any P1 SDK incident.

Notes & future work:
- Integrate delta-runner as a pre-merge CI job for PRs that touch runtime or serialization layers.
- Expand golden corpus to include multi-lingual streaming traces.

If you find gaps or need access to goldens/telemetry, ping the doc owner or eng-sre on Slack (#devx-oncall).
